about: Shah Investor's Home Limited is a retail stock broker with over three decades of operations, offering equity, derivatives, commodity and currency broking, margin trading facility (MTF), depository services and mutual fund/PMS distribution under the 'Shah Investors' brand. It serves about 85,422 clients (38,189 active) through 11 branches and 181 authorised persons, mostly in Gujarat (96% of active clients) and Maharashtra. It is a member of NSE, BSE and MCX and a depository participant with NSDL.
headquarters: Ahmedabad, Gujarat (registered office at GIFT City, Gandhinagar)

objects.purpose: Funding working capital requirements of the Company (mainly to expand the Margin Trading Facility book)
General corporate purposes (capped at 25% of gross proceeds)

promoters.background: Family-run broker. Chairman Upendra Shah and Purnima Shah have about 30 years in broking, Tanmay Shah (MD) about 20 years and Trupti Shah over 17 years. Promoters are not selling shares in the issue (fresh issue only).

concentration.note: Geographic concentration: Gujarat is 93.74% of broking revenue and 96.15% of active clients; broking is 64.78% of FY26 revenue.

litigation_note: No criminal or material civil cases against the company. SEBI penalised the company Rs 4 lakh (Feb 2026) for client-fund upstreaming lapses; SEBI cancelled its Investment Adviser registration (Sep 2025); SFIO summoned erstwhile director Utpal Shah (Aug 2026) over a market-maker client, Kushal Tradelink. Contingent liabilities Rs 64.25 crore (Rs 60 crore bank guarantees, Rs 4.25 crore tax demand).
strengths: Over 30 years in broking with 85,422 clients, 38,189 active clients and 181 authorised persons across Gujarat and Maharashtra.
Loyal client base: 72.61% of active clients have been with the company for more than 5 years.
Very low leverage: borrowings of about Rs 18 crore against Rs 180 crore net worth (debt/equity 0.10).
Healthy margins: FY26 EBITDA margin 30.24% and PAT margin 18.24%, well above peer SMC Global's PAT margin of 5.41%.
Digital shift: share of brokerage from digital platforms rose from 17.61% in FY24 to 42.62% in FY26.
MTF book grew 117% to Rs 20.96 crore in FY26 and reached Rs 54.2 crore by Aug 2026, with 0.00% reported MTF default rate.
New growth avenues: algo-trading platform (NSE approval Aug 2026), GIFT City global investing arm and a Category III AIF registration.
Experienced promoter-managers with 17 to 30 years in stock broking and depository services.

risks.title: Heavy dependence on broking and on Gujarat
risks.detail: Broking gives 64.78% of FY26 revenue and Gujarat contributes 93.74% of broking revenue; broking revenue fell from Rs 64.91 crore to Rs 46.30 crore in FY26.

risks.title: Revenue and profit fell in FY26
risks.detail: Revenue dropped 24.18% to Rs 71.48 crore and PAT fell about 43.5% to Rs 13.20 crore; RoNW slid from 13.91% to 7.35%.

risks.title: Negative operating cash flow
risks.detail: Operating cash flow was negative Rs 19.70 crore in FY26 and negative Rs 31.86 crore in FY25, after a positive Rs 110.19 crore in FY24.

risks.title: SEBI client-fund and regulatory actions
risks.detail: SEBI found client funds were not upstreamed on 18 of 30 sample dates and imposed a Rs 4 lakh penalty; Investment Adviser registration was cancelled and SFIO has summoned an ex-director.

risks.title: MTF exposure exceeded the permitted limit
risks.detail: MTF book was 103.24% of the permissible 50% of eligible net worth at Mar-26 (Rs 20.96 crore vs Rs 20.30 crore limit); IPO money is meant to scale MTF, raising credit risk.

risks.title: Missing and erroneous corporate records
risks.detail: Several RoC forms and share-transfer documents going back to 1994 cannot be traced, and MGT-7 filings had shareholding errors; regulatory action is possible.

risks.title: High working capital needs and IPO use not appraised
risks.detail: Net working capital rose from Rs 39.63 crore to Rs 63.41 crore (standalone); the whole Rs 60 crore object is working capital and has not been appraised by any bank or institution.

risks.title: Contingent liabilities and reliance on authorised persons
risks.detail: Contingent liabilities of Rs 64.25 crore (mostly Rs 60 crore bank guarantees) and heavy reliance on 181 authorised persons for whom the company can be held liable.

notes: Restated consolidated FY24-FY26 (Mar year-end); source in Rs lakh converted to Rs crore. PAT is profit attributable to owners (KPI table); EPS, ROCE, RoNW, RoE, margins, debt/equity are as reported in the RHP. Borrowings are 'Borrowings (other than debt securities)'. cash_and_bank = cash equivalents + other bank balances. Net worth and reserves are attributable to owners (exclude NCI). Price band, issue size in Rs, post-issue shares and P/E at issue price are blank in the RHP. Fresh issue 53,99,200 shares, no OFS. Peer face values were garbled in the table so left null; peer P/E uses NSE close of 31-Aug-2026. Pre-issue promoter holding 60.97% excludes promoter group relatives/HUFs. The risk index covered only 67 of 102 risk factors; litigation details came from the full RHP.
